scenes.heading: Operators
scenes.narration: In Airflow, operators are the reusable templates that define what a single task actually does.

scenes.heading: Kinds of operators
bullets: Action operators run work, like Python or Bash.
Transfer operators move data between systems.
Deferrable operators free up workers while waiting.
Each task is one instantiated operator.
scenes.narration: Action operators perform the real work, such as executing a script or a SQL statement. Transfer operators specialize in moving data from one place to another. Deferrable operators release their worker slot while idle, and every task in a DAG is simply one operator instance.

scenes.heading: Instantiating operators as tasks
scenes.code:
from airflow.operators.bash import BashOperator
from airflow.providers.postgres.operators.postgres import PostgresOperator

sync = BashOperator(
    task_id="sync_files",
    bash_command="aws s3 sync s3://raw /data/raw",
)

load = PostgresOperator(
    task_id="load_staging",
    sql="INSERT INTO staging SELECT * FROM external;",
)
scenes.narration: Each operator becomes a concrete task by passing a unique task id and its configuration. The Bash operator runs a shell command to sync files, while the Postgres operator executes SQL against a database. Choosing the right operator means you write configuration rather than boilerplate integration code.

scenes.heading: Operators vs sensors
scenes.narration: Operators do work and then finish, producing a result. Sensors instead wait for something to become true, like a file appearing, before letting the pipeline continue. Both are tasks, but one acts while the other watches.

scenes.text: Operators are prebuilt task templates that let you configure common actions and integrations instead of coding them from scratch.
scenes.narration: Reaching for the right operator keeps your DAGs declarative, so tasks describe intent rather than plumbing.
